- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast growth to 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If supply net is negative and event count is high, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance or add 1–3% downward drift.
- For 30d forecasts with high event density and negative supply net, model tends to lag true price decline; apply 1–3 day lag correction (shift forecast down by 0.5–1.5% per day).
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish → bearish transitions, model overreacts to sentiment; dampen forecast slope by 20–40% during sentiment shifts.
